subject: Phased expansion ratecard and co-term approval
thread_summary: MediQ is asking for a phased expansion pricing matrix and co-terming path for mid-contract uplift. Internal team proposed a staged ratecard and a limited one-time concession; procurement timeline and legal signer were confirmed by the customer.
messages:
From: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@mediq.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@mediq.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Expansion pricing for Q4 (mid-contract uplift)

Hi Jordan —

We ran into higher than expected volume this quarter and are planning a staged expansion across three product teams starting Oct 1. We have an existing subscription that co-terms next June, so procurement asked whether we can do a mid-contract uplift that aligns to the existing co-term (no extension).

Can you send a phased ratecard (month-by-month for the first 6 months) and suggested invoice cadence? Also need any standard language we require for a co-term amendment and an estimate for lead times (SOW / billing).

Rough ask: +3x token volume in Q4 and a second phase in Q1 that adds fine-tuning slots. We are targetting a PO by Sep 15 if numbers look reasonable.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Turner
Head of Platform Integrations
MediQ Health

P.S. looping Carlos (finance) — he will coordinate PO/terms on our side.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@mediq.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@mediq.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Sep 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expansion pricing for Q4 (mid-contract uplift)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context, this is helpful.

High-level plan (attached ratecard + SOW draft):
- Phase 1 (Oct): 1.5x token uplift — short ramp pricing (month 1 premium then normalized months 2–3)
- Phase 2 (Nov–Dec): move to committed uplift (annualized rate for year-1 blended into invoice)
- Phase 3 (Q1): add fine-tuning seats as a per-seat add-on (tiered discounts at 5/10/20% based on committed units)

We will produce a month-by-month CSV for the first 6 months and an SOW draft that mirrors your co-term to avoid redoing contract dates. Attachments: MediQ_growth_ratecard_v1.xlsx, SOW_draft_MediQ_v0.2.pdf.

Question for procurement/legal: who will sign the amendment on your side? If you can share the procurement contact that speeds things up. Also, what invoice cadence do you prefer (monthly vs quarterly)?

I’ll loop Naomi (your AM) to nail the price bands and confirm any one-time onboarding credit we can offer.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0191

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@mediq.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@mediq.com>
Date: Sun, 06 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expansion pricing for Q4 (mid-contract uplift)

Hi Sarah / Jordan —

Thanks — I took Jordan’s draft and mapped it to three concrete pricing bands in the attached spreadsheet (MediQ_growth_ratecard_v1.xlsx) and included a short Annex A co-term template (AnnexA_co-term-template.docx) that legal can use to create an amendment without pushing your primary term date. Quick bullets:

- Phase 1 (Oct): ramp pricing = list price + 8% premium month 1, then list price with 2% uplift month 2–3 to cover burst capacity.
- Phase 2 (Nov–Dec): if committed uplift hits >= 2.5x, apply a blended 12% discount on the incremental units for the remainder of the co-term year.
- Phase 3 (Q1): fine-tuning seats priced at $4,500/seat/month, with tiered discounts at 5% (5–9 seats), 10% (10–24 seats), 20% (25+ seats).

One-time incentives we can include to help close quickly: a 5% onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) and free priority support for 90 days. Any concession beyond that needs manager approval — I’ve flagged potential for a one-time additional concession if procurement can commit to an accelerated PO (by Sep 15).

Invoice cadence options: monthly (standard) or quarterly with net-30. If you need cashflow smoothing we can invoice monthly but bill quarterly in arrears — we’ll note that in SOW.

Attached: MediQ_growth_ratecard_v1.xlsx, AnnexA_co-term-template.docx, SOW_draft_MediQ_v0.2.pdf

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Account Manager — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Expansion pricing for Q4 (mid-contract uplift)

Jordan / Naomi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments look sensible. A few clarifications before we sign off internally:

1) Can we shorten Phase 1 lead time from 30 days to 18 days for the first wave? We have an objective to get the first product team live before Oct 20.
2) Procurement prefers quarterly billing if possible; monthly would be acceptable with a net-30.
3) Please update the SOW to include our procurement contact for signature: procurement@mediq.com and show estimated PO by Sep 15 — that’s our target.

If you can update the SOW and the ratecard (shortened Phase 1 lead) I’ll route this to legal and procurement — Carlos will handle the PO.

Best,
Sarah

Condition: procurement must provide a PO by Sep 15 and the signed co-term annex.

Jordan / Naomi — please update the SOW and the finance ticket, and record the concession in HubSpot (Deal: DEAL-4721) so discounts are captured for renewals reporting.
